- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by 5–10% of recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often lags; forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.20 → 0.00 → 0.20), model overfits trend; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment).
